title: Sequence Compactifier: hierarchical reservation + fragment shedding for padding reduction
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a 'Sequence Compactifier' micro-batcher extension that reduces pad tokens across mixed-length workloads by combining a hierarchical reservation slab for low-latency requests with a fragment-shedding stage during prefill-to-decode transition. The feature should provide kernel-selection hints to the runtime (dense vs sparse attention kernels) and integrate with the prefill scheduler to preserve latency SLOs for short requests while reclaiming padded capacity from long requests.
acceptance_criteria: Reduce average padded tokens per request by >= 30% on the synthetic webchat trace (2025-10 production sample)
No regression in generation quality: BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity delta <= 0.5% on the prompt evaluation suite
P95 latency for 'short' requests (<=64 tokens) does not increase by more than 5% under mixed load
End-to-end integration tests covering kernel hint propagation, prefill reservation fallback, and partial-shedding correctness
Feature toggled by config + rollout via canary; ability to force-off per-customer
tasks: Design sketch & trade-off doc (owner: Aisha) - complete
Prototype sequence compactifier in Python scheduler - Diego
Microbench kernels: add hint path to runtime to prefer sparse attention for fragmented batches - Eng runtime team
Benchmark runs across 8 GPU nodes (mixed-length workload) and capture pad savings + latency profile
Add integration tests and QA: correctness for KV cache, prompt prefixes, and token bookkeeping
Rollout plan: dev -> canary (10% traffic) -> tiered increase with automatic rollback if SLO breached
decision_log: Chose hierarchical reservation (small slab for latency-sensitive short requests + pooled slab for bulk) vs single-pass trimming because it provides predictable tail-latency control
Fragment shedding (dropping low-entropy tail tokens from padding candidates) selected after QA showed negligible quality impact on conversational prompts
Will expose kernel-selection hint instead of forcing kernel to allow runtime to respect hardware affinities and avoid brittle scheduling decisions
Prefill reservation size defaults tuned per model family (gpt-large/llama-like) and derived from 7-day traffic histogram
benchmark_notes: Prototype run (2025-11-12) on staging: avg padded tokens/request down 33% vs baseline; cost proxy (GPU-ms) down ~18%
Observed small P99 increase (+7%) in synthetic all-long workload when reservation was set too large; addressed via adaptive cap in scheduler
Kernel hinting end-to-end measured 6% better throughput when runtime honored sparse-attn hint for fragmented batches on A100 configs
Quality eval: embedding cosine similarity median delta -0.2% on conv-eval set after fragment shedding (within tolerance)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: unfair scheduling could starve long requests; Mitigation: fairness timer that forces reservation relinquish after X ms
Risk: fragment shedding may break structured-output prompts; Mitigation: prompt whitelist via metadata and conservative shedding heuristics
Risk: kernel hint mismatch causing suboptimal runtime choices; Mitigation: telemetry to detect ignored hints and adaptive fallback to legacy packer
